svg.text: NEXUS - STM32 carrier and 5 V split board: soldering and wiring
Kit perfboards (BOM 5.11), 2.54 grid · Boards A and B, both 5×7 cm (18 × 24 holes), under P1 and P2, 5.9 mm apart · Board C 3×7 cm (10 × 24), the 5 V split · MEC-08 / MEC-15 / HW-19
Hole names: board·hole, as PRINTED on the kit board - letters A-X along the 70 mm side, numbers across (1-18 on A and B, 1-10 on C), A1 bottom-left with the print readable, as every view shows it.

Header row n (pins 2n-1, 2n) is letter X for row 1 back to A for row 24 · P1 odd pins A·A10-X10 (outboard), even A·A9-X9 · P2 odd B·A12-X12 (inboard), even B·A11-X11 (UM1472 Fig. 10) · fixings are F1-F6, never hole names.

Parts on the component side, every wire on the solder side. Bare tinned links only where drawn bare; everything else is insulated, soldered at both ends, so crossings are fine. Nothing on the Discovery footprint stands taller than a resistor.
A + B COMPONENT SIDE (from above, front LEFT)
P1 on the vehicle right (top), P2 on the vehicle left (bottom) - chassis-layout convention
A + B SOLDER SIDE (turned over about the long axis)
front still LEFT, so P2 is now on TOP and every column reads upside down
module H / L links in at V6, V4
front ◀ boards 70 mm + Discovery overhang = 98 mm ▶ rear (fascia)
overall width 106 mm · F1-F4: ⌀3.2 holes onto existing plate-2 holes, 10 mm M2.5 standoffs
front ◀ boards 70 mm + Discovery overhang = 98 mm ▶ rear (fascia)
overall width 106 mm · F1-F4: ⌀3.2 holes onto existing plate-2 holes, 10 mm M2.5 standoffs
across the plate-2 waist, x 85.5-115.5: letter A at the vehicle right, 10 to the front · socket opening faces the vehicle right
C SOLDER SIDE (turned over about the long axis)
spines in bare tinned 18 AWG, TO STM32 in 18 AWG (thick), the CC network in thin wire
Socket first: meter CC1 and CC2 to V and to G, all four open - a socket with its own Rd (5.1k) or Rp cannot be the source.
Fit the F5 pan-head screw (D6) before the socket: the body rides 2.5 mm up on its flange, over the head. Ties through 3 mm holes at B9 / B2 and F9 / F2, the second one over the pigtail.
C TO STM32 → B 5V IN (B·D2) → P2-3 / P2-4 (W12 = W11)
socket red V (C·G10) · C1 + (L10) · R1 / R2 tops (L4 = L2 → O10)
C spine c → B 5V IN GND → spine j → P2-1/2 · CAN GND · XCVR GND
bare along X: B·X18 → A·X1 → X9 = X10 (P1-2, P1-1) · spine 14 → 6V IN, C2, SERVO, I2C
XCVR 3V3 (B·L5) · bare along V: B·V18 → A·V1 → V8, never V9 · → I2C-A VCC (D16)
link → B·V6 → CAN H (X6) · R3 120R → TERM
green CC1 (C·G4) → R1 10k → 5 V · yellow CC2 (G2) → R2 10k → 5 V (source Rp, HW-02)
Bauer 50 W via SW2, 18 AWG pair (HW-17)
socket on C, pigtail soldered: red G10, black G8, green G4, yellow G2 · C-to-C data cable to FRDM J1
white and blue cut short, each insulated on its own - never twisted together
servo plug: signal to A·K16 (rear), brown/black to M16
INA226 GND, VCC, SCL, SDA - F-F leads, signal only
motor module SCL / SDA / GND - never its 5 V pin
twisted H, L + GND to DE-9 stub and FRDM P12 (HW-09, HW-18)
jumper ON = this end terminated (120 Ω), OFF = open
5×7 board · 2 × 1×25 female · 1 × 2p terminal · 1×3 + 1×3 + 1×4 male · C2 470µF · R4 1k
5×7 board · 2 × 1×25 + 1 × 1×4 female · 3p + 2p terminal · 1×2 male + jumper cap · R3 120Ω
3×7 board · 2 × 2p terminal · USB-C socket (5.1), 2 zip ties · C1 470µF · R1, R2 10k
caps: 2 of the 5 in 3.14 · resistors: 3.21 · module: 4.1 · headers, terminals: 5.11
thin copper hook-up wire, 22-26 AWG, and bare tinned copper for the spines and bridges - not the CCA Dupont leads (5.7)
plate 2 M2.5 hole (169.88, 14.24) - mark from the plate
plate 2 M2.5 hole (169.88, 100.24) - under the module
plate 2 M3 hole (99.24, 38.76), ⌀3.18 - under the socket
All six: ⌀3.2 in the board, M2.5 × 10 standoff, M2.5 screws, washer in the ⌀3.18 holes.
Header row 1 at chassis x 181.20 · A outboard edge y 5.11 · B outboard edge y 110.99 · gap y 55.11-60.99.
CHECK BEFORE THE IRON IS HOT
1 Count the holes: A and B need 18 × 24, C 10 × 24. The drawing assumes the usual kit counts; a board one row short moves everything.
2 Cut four 1×25 strips from the 40-pin female headers and snip the 25th tail of each flush with the body. Dry-fit them on the Discovery,
boards A and B under them: pins on A·A10-X10 / A9-X9 and B·A12-X12 / A11-X11, and header row 25 past A, on the margin with no hole under it.
3 Solder the sockets WITH THE DISCOVERY PLUGGED IN - it is the only thing that sets the 53.34 mm between A and B. Tack two corners, check, finish.
4 Measure the SN65HVD230 module: outline, pin order, and CANH-CANL unpowered. ~120 Ω means it carries its own terminator - remove it,
so TERM alone decides. Pin order drawn is the BOM's (3V3, GND, CRX, CTX): wire the socket to what the module actually prints.
5 The kit terminals may be 5.0 mm, not 5.08: the 3p CAN block spans 10.0 vs 10.16 mm of holes. Push it in; do not drill.
6 Before the Discovery goes back in: 5 V to GND not shorted · 6 V rail isolated from 5 V and 3V3 · 5 V on B·W12 / W11 only · nothing on B·U12 (PH0) · A·V9 (P1-4 VDD) not on 3V3.
7 Fixings: drill F1, F2, F5 and F6 on the grid first. Screw A and B down with the Discovery in, then mark F3 and F4 from under the
plate through its holes, lift the carrier and drill them. No standoff may touch a bare spine: check each one before the screw goes in.
The kit's 7×9 (24 × 30) takes all 100 pins, but the Discovery
covers it, so no terminal or cap would have anywhere to go. Two 5×7s
leave them outboard and meet 5.9 mm apart: each bridge is bare wire
soldered along its row, 12.7 mm unsupported. Row 25 is GND only.
Both 470 µF caps and every resistor are now on a board. C2 sits at
the servo header, where the stall current is. C1, R1 and R2 are on
board C, which is the 5 V split: the FRDM's amps never cross the
STM32 carrier, and the Rp pair sits beside the pigtail it serves.
The carrier's one ground lead is B 5V IN GND, back through C to the
(−) WAGO (HW-06). The 6 V servo rail reaches C2 and SERVO only
(HW-11). 3V3 comes from P2-5/6, never P1 VDD (JP1): 100 mA ceiling,
the transceiver and INA226 logic only. R4 guards PE9 if the servo
plug goes on one pin off.

Geometry: UM1472 Fig. 10 (board 66 × 97, outer rows 53.34 apart, 6.33 in from each edge, first row 33.82 from the CN1 edge) · Pins: UM1472 Table 5 and the P1/P2 schematic · P2-3/4 = 5V, P2-5/6 = 3V, P2-7 = PH0
Decisions: MEC-08 (carrier) · MEC-15 (kit boards) · HW-19 (5 V split board, selectable termination) · HW-06 · HW-09 · HW-11 · HW-18 · SVG is the master - PDFs are generated once the design is frozen.
